subject: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, structured output, and routing policy options
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ashley Chen <ashley@vantagecare.io>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@vantagecare.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, structured output, and routing policy options

Hi Ashley / Miguel —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap + pragmatic next steps so we keep momentum into a technical kickoff: your product team sounded excited about integrating Redwood for triage automation and patient-message generation. The things we agreed to validate next:

- SDK & auth: your infra prefers a service-account flow (server-to-server) over embedding API keys in app bundles. We should confirm whether VantageCare wants OAuth 2.0 service accounts (recommended) or a managed API-key rotation approach.
- Routing & policies: you highlighted strict latency targets for synchronous triage (p95 < 220ms) and a higher-latency batch path for analytics. We sketched a routing policy that prioritizes lowest-cost model meeting latency SLO, with a fallback chain to smaller models during capacity spikes.
- Structured output / tool calling: you’ll want the model to emit JSON for the triage payload (intent, urgency, suggested tags) and optionally call a reranker/embeddings-based similarity check for prior-case retrieval.

Attachments: I’ve attached a one-page integration checklist and a sample SDK config that maps to the points above (auth examples, routing policy stub, structured-output schema).

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Confirm preferred auth approach (service account / OAuth or API key + rotation).
2) Share a small sample payload and the fields you need in the triage JSON (one pager will do).
3) Which regions do you expect traffic from? We’ll pre-provision capacity in us-west and us-east if you expect cross-coast traffic.

Proposed next step: 45-minute technical kickoff next Tuesday (Dec 7) where MK can walk through SDK auth examples and routing policy templates. I’ve tentatively placed a calendar invite (attached) for Dec 7 10am PT — please confirm.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0114

Attachments: integration-checklist.pdf (1 page), sample-config.yaml (snippet)

From: Ashley Chen <ashley@vantagecare.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@vantagecare.io>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, structured output, and routing policy options

Thanks, Irene —

This is great. Quick answers:
- Auth: we prefer a service-account / OAuth 2.0 flow. We have an internal KMS and would like Redwood to accept signed JWTs issued by our identity provider (Auth0 for now). Can you confirm the expected token lifetime and whether you need an OIDC discovery URL?
- Payload: I’ll loop in product with the sample fields, but primary ones are: patient_id, message_text, triage_intent, urgency_score (0-1), suggested_tags (list), confidence_pct. We also want an optional metadata block for original_message_id and region.
- Regions: majority US-east, with occasional US-west spikes.

One more ask: for reranking, we have a small vector DB and we'd like Redwood to call a reranker after generation that uses embeddings to re-score candidates. Can you outline how the reranker step fits into the SDK flow (sync vs async)?

Confirming the Dec 7 10am PT kickoff — Miguel and I will be there.

— Ashley
Ashley Chen
Head of Product, VantageCare
ashley@vantagecare.io

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ashley Chen <ashley@vantagecare.io>
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@vantagecare.io>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, structured output, and routing policy options

Hi all —

Following up with technical details to help you evaluate the SDK flow and routing policy options before the kickoff. I kept this intentionally concrete so your infra team can eyeball compatibility.

1) Auth & SDK initialization
- Redwood supports JWT-bearer service accounts (recommended) and API keys. For JWTs we expect a standard RSA-signed JWT with 'iss' and 'sub' matching your service account and an 'exp' up to 1 hour. If you require shorter lifetimes, we support token exchange where your system mints short-lived tokens and Redwood accepts them via our token-exchange endpoint.
- OIDC: we can accept tokens issued by any OIDC-compliant IdP; we only need your jwks_uri for key rotation and an issuer identifier.
- SDK: server-side SDK initialization looks like
  - client = RedwoodClient.from_jwt({"jwt": "<SIGNED_JWT>"})
  - fallback: client = RedwoodClient.from_api_key("<ROTATING_KEY>")

2) Routing policy primitives (what we propose)
- policy priority list: {region_affinity -> latency_slo -> cost_ceiling -> model_compatibility}
- Region routing: traffic can be routed by origin IP region header. For your case: prefer us-east nodes, fallback to us-west.
- Latency SLO enforcement: set p95 target 220ms; policy evaluates slow-path models and can short-circuit to a cached response if prefix cache hits (saves cost).
- Fallback chain example: base model (redwood-large-quant) -> lightweight model (redwood-medium-quant) -> cached template response (if > 75% cache hit) -> degraded mode (summary only)
- Cost ceilings: you can set per-route max token rate or per-request cost budget; requests exceeding budget get routed to cheaper model variants.

3) Structured output & reranker integration
- Structured output: we recommend using our typed-json schema option. You pass a JSON schema and the runtime validates & returns JSON. Example: {"triage": {"intent": "string", "urgency": "number", "tags": ["string"]}}
- Tool-calling / reranker: two patterns
  a) sync inline: generation -> produce candidates -> call your reranker endpoint (we do a single HTTP call with batched embeddings) -> return best candidate. This keeps the end-to-end latency in-path (ok for p95 when reranker is fast).
  b) async: generation returns candidate list and an event id; reranker runs off-path and updates a record (you poll or receive webhook). Use async for heavy reranking or large external DB scans.
- Embeddings: Redwood can return embeddings per candidate; you can compute similarity on your side and send back the chosen candidate id for final rendering. Alternatively, we can host a reranker function as a small webhook you provide.

4) SDK examples for retry and fallback
- Our SDK exposes a policy DSL:
  - router = client.router().with_region_affinity("us-east").with_latency_slo(220).with_fallbacks(["redwood-large-quant", "redwood-medium-quant"])
  - response = router.generate(prompt, schema=triage_schema, reranker_webhook="https://hooks.vantagecare.io/rerank")

Notes & tradeoffs:
- Inline reranking adds latency but simplifies correctness (one round-trip). If your reranker is microsecond-fast (in-memory vector lookup) it’s viable for sync triage. For heavy DB scans, prefer async.
- Cache & prefix strategies reduce cost but require consistent prompt shaping to be effective.
- We recommend rate-limiting by user/session to control accidental cost spikes.

Irene — I attached a slightly expanded sample-config.yaml with the router stub and an example reranker webhook. Happy to walk through this at the kickoff.

Thanks —
Markus
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ashley Chen <ashley@vantagecare.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@vantagecare.io>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, structured output, and routing policy options

Perfect — this is exactly what we needed. Quick confirmation of next steps and owners: 

- Ashley / Miguel: share the one-pager with exact triage JSON fields and representative sample messages by EOD Friday (owner: Ashley).
- VantageCare infra: confirm jwks_uri and whether the IdP will issue short-lived JWTs (owner: Miguel).
- Redwood: we’ll prepare a targeted demo of the server-side SDK auth flow and the policy DSL, plus a short benchmark that shows p95 latencies for inline rerank vs async rerank on us-east nodes (owner: Markus / Irene).

I’ve updated the HubSpot deal (link in metadata) with the kickoff agenda and attached the invite — please accept when you get a chance. During the kickoff we’ll also allocate a sandbox key and a small dedicated capacity burst for a 2-week POC so you can validate latency/cost tradeoffs.

If anything urgent pops up before the meeting, Slack me in #solutions-redwood or email. Looking forward to the demo.

Best —
Irene
